content: Nabidh was a beverage known for its intoxicating properties. According to a narration by Abu Hurayrah, he recounted that he was aware of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) observing fasts. On a day when the Prophet was not fasting, Abu Hurayrah prepared nabidh in a pumpkin and brought it to him. However, by the time it was presented, the drink had fermented. The Prophet instructed him to throw it against a wall, stating that such a drink was associated with those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day. During the final moments of Umar ibn al-Khattab's life, as he was severely affected by a wound, his physician inquired about which type of alcohol he preferred to drink. Umar expressed his preference for nabidh. Consequently, this drink was administered to him. Yahya ibn Said narrated from Abd ar-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, who reported that Aslam, a servant of Umar ibn al-Khattab, once visited Abdullah ibn Ayyash al-Makhzumi. During this visit, Aslam noticed that Abdullah had nabidh with him while traveling to Mecca. Aslam remarked that Umar ibn al-Khattab was fond of this drink. In response, Abdullah carried a large drinking bowl filled with nabidh and presented it to Umar. Umar brought the drink close to himself, raised his head, and remarked that the drink was good. He then consumed some of it and passed the bowl to the man seated to his right. The Muslim writer Ibn Fadlan documented that nabidh was consumed by the Vikings. It was reportedly brewed over a period of ten days and was likely alcohol-based. The drink may have included additional substances such as henbane, cannabis, or opium. Ibn Fadlan described a ritual in which this drink was given to a female slave who was later sacrificed through strangulation and stabbing during a ship burial ceremony.
